name: Sticky braai ribs
summary: Pork spare ribs baked low and slow until tender, then finished over hot coals with a sweet, tangy basting until sticky and charred at the edges.
about: Basted pork ribs are a steakhouse and braai favourite across South Africa. Cooking them gently first and finishing them on the fire is how home braaiers get meat that comes off the bone and a glaze that caramelises instead of burning. Serve with chips, coleslaw or a potato salad.
steps: Heat the oven to 160 °C (140 °C fan). Season the rib racks all over with the salt and pepper and lay them meaty side up in a large roasting tin.
Pour the water into the tin, cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the meat is tender and has started to shrink back from the ends of the bones.
While the ribs bake, stir all the basting ingredients together in a small pot over medium heat and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened and glossy. Set aside to cool.
Light the fire and let it burn down to medium-hot coals, when you can hold your hand at grid height for about 4 seconds.
Lift the ribs out of the tin and brush both sides thickly with the basting.

Braai the racks for 12 to 15 minutes, turning and basting every 2 to 3 minutes, until the basting is sticky and the edges are dark and charred in places. Move them to a cooler spot if the sugar starts to burn.
Rest the racks on a board for 5 minutes, then cut between the bones into single ribs and serve with any leftover basting warmed for dipping.
prepNote: Bake the ribs and make the basting up to a day ahead; keep both in the fridge and braai just before serving.
